questions.stem: The dilated endoplasmic reticulum is called?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dohle bodies
  • In sepsis or severe inflammatory disorders (e.g., Kawasaki disease), leukocytosis can have morphologic changes in the neutrophils:
  • Cytoplasmic vacuoles
  • Toxic granules, which are coarser and darker than the normal neutrophilic granules, represent abnormal azurophilic (primary) granules.
  • Döhle bodies are patches of the dilated endoplasmic reticulum that appear as sky-blue cytoplasmic “puddles”

Döhle bodies are seen in

  1. Myelodysplastic syndromes
  2. Sepsis
  3. Chediak Higashi syndrome

Reactive changes in neutrophils. Neutrophils containing coarse purple cytoplasmic granules (toxic granulations) and blue cytoplasmic patches of dilated endoplasmic reticulum (Döhle bodies) (arrow) are observed in this peripheral blood smear prepared from a patient with bacterial sepsis.





Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 588, 620

questions.stem: The mutation is seen in systemic mastocytosis:
questions.solutionHtml:
c-kit point mutation
  • The mutation commonly seen in systemic mastocytosis is a c-kit point mutation.
  • The c-kit gene codes for a receptor tyrosine kinase that is expressed on the surface of mast cells. In systemic mastocytosis, there is a mutation in the c-kit gene that leads to the constitutive activation of the c-kit receptor, resulting in the abnormal proliferation and accumulation of mast cells in various tissues.
  • Mutations in other genes, such as FGFR1, BCR-ABL, and JAK2, are associated with other myeloproliferative neoplasms but are not commonly associated with systemic mastocytosis.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 622

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a chronic myeloproliferative disorder?
questions.solutionHtml:
Essential thrombocytopenia
  • Myeloid metaplasia is another name for myelofibrosis.
  • Essential ThromboCYTOSIS is Chronic Myeloproliferative Disorder (not thrombocytopenia)


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 621, 622
